title: Generalizable Multi-Pass Training of Ads Recommendation Models with Foundation Model Guidance

problem.claim: High-capacity ads recommendation CTR models often overfit after one training epoch, with further passes degrading generalization by memorizing noise in high-variance click labels.

gap.claim: Standard training based on noisy click-label likelihood does not support effective generalizable multi-pass training.

contributions.claim: TeMPO is a framework for generalizable multi-pass recommendation-model training using supervision from a teacher recommendation Foundation Model.
The framework maximizes joint likelihood of click labels and teacher representational knowledge through task-loss and teacher-guided alignment objectives.
TeMPO uses a two-stage optimization strategy to stabilize multi-pass learning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Theoretical analysis reports that distillation acts as complexity regularization and yields tighter generalization bounds than standard empirical risk minimization under noisy labels.
Experiments on public benchmarks and Meta's production-scale ads application report that TeMPO allows additional training passes to improve rather than degrade performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: One-epoch overfitting limits additional training passes for high-capacity ads recommendation CTR models.
TeMPO addresses the problem by using supervision from a teacher recommendation Foundation Model.
The method supplements noisy click-label likelihood with teacher-knowledge modeling and alignment objectives.
A two-stage optimization strategy is used to stabilize multi-pass learning.
The abstract reports theoretical and experimental support for improved multi-pass performance.

source_observation.claim: Additional passes over noisy click-label data can degrade generalization through memorization.

interpretation.claim: Training objectives that incorporate richer supervisory signals may regularize repeated optimization over noisy labels.

application.claim: For noisy-label recommendation training, consider combining task supervision with teacher-guided representation alignment when extending training beyond one pass.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond the reported recommendation settings, datasets, or teacher-model configurations.

unknowns: Exact benchmark datasets, evaluation metrics, and quantitative performance changes are unspecified.
